DECISION = Option A: the provider hosts an android.view.SurfaceView inside the WebView (a ViewGroup) and feeds NWeb that holder's Surface. Static finding: our runtime does NOT composite a bare window node's own surface (cc-t3 window14 = display stays on launcher); only a self-drawing child RSSurfaceNode AddChild'd to the window is GPU-composited -- and a SurfaceView already gets exactly that via [STAGE2-SURFACEVIEW] -> oh_rs_get_child_surface_window -> 'AdapterSurfaceView' (SetHardwareEnabled XCOM, AddChild, child->GetSurface()). AOSP SurfaceView reaches it via BLASTBufferQueue/SurfaceControl; oh_anw_get_oh(holder.getSurface()) resolves to that child node's producer; FlutterSurfaceView uses it (U14 localsend hilog AdapterSurfaceView x25, EGLSurface non-zero). WebView extends AbsoluteLayout so it can host a SurfaceView. A reuses the proven composited-child path + free View-framework geometry/visibility/z-order sync (no native dep); B (native mode-32 child node + hand-synced JNI) is the fallback. Deliver: NWebSurfaceLifecycle (android-free, unit-tested 12/12 -- defer create to surfaceCreated, deferred url/settings, resize, destroy/recreate) + OhNWebSurfaceHost (glue) + offline test; B's sync-JNI sketch for cc-t3 mode 32. Offline, no board.** |
